title: Religion is sincere counsel
hook: religion is sincere goodwill: to Allah, His book, His messenger, leaders and all people
tomorrow: one hadith gets clipped and shared to scare people. what does it say?

segments.voice: A week of foundations. What did I intend? He came to teach you your religion. Built on five. Written, and still we strive. Keep it as it came. And yesterday, at the edge of the gray: guard the heart. Now, one word for the whole thing.
screen: `WHAT DID I INTEND? · HE CAME TO TEACH YOU · BUILT ON FIVE` → `STILL WE STRIVE · KEEP IT AS IT CAME · GUARD THE HEART`

segments.voice: A friend turns around in the fitting room: be honest, does this look okay? The answer that helps is neither flattery nor a takedown. It's the one that actually wants her to walk out looking good. Yesterday's question: the whole religion in one word? Tamim al-Dari reports that the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, gave exactly that. Religion is nasihah. The companions asked the obvious thing: to whom?
screen: `BE HONEST: DOES THIS LOOK OKAY?` → `RELIGION IS NASIHAH.` → `TO WHOM?`

segments.voice: To Allah, to His Book, to His Messenger, to the leaders of the Muslims, and to their ordinary people. Nasihah is sincere goodwill: wanting the good for someone, and meaning it all the way through. Al-Nawawi's commentary opens each one up. Toward Allah, it's sincerity in worship. Toward His Book, reading it and living by it. Toward His Messenger, honoring and following him. Toward leaders, wanting them to do right and telling them honestly when they don't. And toward ordinary people, wishing them well, guiding them kindly, covering their faults. One to tell a friend tonight: in this hadith, advice is only one way goodwill shows. The word is bigger than advice. Look back and the whole week has been goodwill: an intention checked, a teacher who asked, a building kept standing, effort beside the decree, worship kept whole, a heart on guard.
screen: `TO ALLAH, HIS BOOK, HIS MESSENGER.` · `TO LEADERS AND ORDINARY PEOPLE.` · `BIGGER THAN ADVICE.` · then, large: `SINCERE GOODWILL.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person who could use an honest word from you, something kind and true they may not have heard. Type it as a message, but don't send it yet. Read it back slowly, and cut anything that's about being right instead of about their good.
screen: `ONE HONEST, KIND WORD.` · `DRAFT IT. DON'T SEND.` · `CUT WHAT'S ABOUT WINNING.`

segments.voice: Nasihah: sincere goodwill, wanting the good for someone. The Prophet called the whole religion by this one word.
Hold on to this one: sincere goodwill, to Allah and to the person right in front of you. Week one of the forty, done.

howItsDone: Muslims treat honest, kind advice as part of the religion itself; teachers stress giving it sincerely and gently, and recommend giving a correction in private.

fork.setup: your friend's band plays a show and the singer was off-key all night. in front of everyone, she asks what you thought. what fits nasihah?
options: name what was good now, and tell her the hard part kindly, later, alone.
tell her everything right away; honesty can't wait for a better moment.
say it was perfect; goodwill means never making a friend feel bad.
fork.reveal: nasihah wants her good: honest enough to help, kind enough to be heard. a quiet word later does both.
